chunks: And it was narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh that he said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام say:

If you enter the mosque while the Imam is in rukuʿ, and you think that if you walk toward him he will raise his head, then say the takbir and perform rukuʿ. Then when he raises his head, perform sajdah in your place. Then if he stands, join the row; and if he sits, then sit in your place, and when he stands, join the row.

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, the place where the congregational salat is being performed
key_terms.بِالصَّفِّ: the prayer row of the congregation
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of rukuʿ, the bowing posture in salat
key_terms.فَكَبِّرْ: say the takbir to enter the prayer

ai.seo_question: How should someone join congregational salat if they enter the mosque while the Imam is in rukuʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains how a latecomer should act when entering congregational salat while the Imam is already in rukuʿ. It gives a practical ruling on joining the prayer without missing the congregational movement and maintaining order in the row.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1148 - It was narrated from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah that He said:
"I heard Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) say:

"If you enter the mosque and the Imam is in the bowing position (ruku'), and you think that if you walk towards him, he will raise his head, then pronounce the takbir (opening supplication) and bow. When the Imam raises his head, prostrate in your place. If the Imam then stands, join the row. If he sits, remain seated in your place, and when he stands again, join the row."
